claim: For the Liu–Du–Zhang–Li–Shi system \(\dot x=ay+xz\), \(\dot y=-bx+yz\), \(\dot z=1-x^2-y^2\), \(\dot w=z(w-1)\) with \(a,b>0\), let \(Q=bx^2+ay^2\). On \(Q>0\), \(I=(w-1)^2/Q\) is an exact first integral and \(w(t)-1=(w(0)-1)\sqrt{Q(t)/Q(0)}\). Every compact ergodic invariant probability measure has support in \(Q>0\), satisfies \(\int z\,d\mu=0\), and has four-dimensional Lyapunov spectrum \(\{\lambda,0,0,-\lambda\}\) for some \(\lambda\ge0\), counting multiplicity. Consequently the exact system has at most one positive Lyapunov exponent on compact recurrent dynamics and cannot be hyperchaotic in the standard two-positive-exponent sense; changes of the initial fourth coordinate with the same \((x,y,z)\) initial condition only rescale the slaved fiber about \(w=1\).
integrity: The vector field and the source's two-positive-exponent hyperchaos claims were checked in the lawful open-access full text. The key differential identities and Jacobian structure are exact and were replayed by a packaged symbolic checker. The Lyapunov-spectrum implication is proved analytically from invariant-subspace, Liouville, and autonomous-flow arguments. No independent audit or external validation is claimed.
limitations: The theorem concerns compact ergodic invariant probability measures of the exact ODE and asymptotic Oseledets exponents. It does not classify noncompact trajectories, prove existence of a physical measure, or certify convergence of any finite-time numerical Lyapunov estimate. The originality search was targeted and cannot exclude unindexed equivalent work.
title: Exact fiber slaving and a no-hyperchaos theorem for a reported four-dimensional hidden-attractor flow
